newsitem.title: USA: Biota flu treatment trial to start in May.
newsitem.headline: Biota flu treatment trial to start in May.

text.p: Biota Holdings Ltd said Monday that Glaxo Wellcome P1c, its partner, will begin Phase III clinical trials of Zanamivir, or GG167, its treatment for influenza this May in Australia.
This southern hemisphere trial will be a part of a worldwide Phase III program which will include two separate pivotal proof of efficacy studies that will begin in the northern hemisphere in October.
Results from the Phase IIB studies from the northern hemisphere, together with those from earlier studies, confirm that Zanamivir is a potentially valuable therapy for influenza, said the company.
The company said Zanamivir will be administered twice daily for five days in these trials, using Glaxo Wellcome's Diskhaler technology for inhaled dosing.
World-wide filing for Zanamivir is planned to take place in the second half of 1998, said the company.
Glaxo is developing Zanamivir as part of an agreement with Biota which also includes commercialization of the drug.
Biota, based in Melbourne, Australia, is primarily engaged in the the discovery of drugs for the treatment of viral respiratory diseases and cancer.
